subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should ordinary external plugins be allowed to invoke Gateway methods registered by other plugins, and if so should access be raw method dispatch, manifest-declared allowlists, or typed capability/service APIs?
rationale: This changes the public Plugin SDK authorization boundary; automation cannot choose which third-party plugins may invoke which Gateway methods or how mutating and sensitive methods are exposed.

options.title: Design a narrow external contract
options.body: Expose only approved or manifest-declared methods/capabilities with caller attribution, trust-tier behavior, docs, and focused contract tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-official only
options.body: Document that community plugins cannot use in-process Gateway RPC dispatch unless promoted to the trusted official install path.

options.title: Allow broad raw dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method-string caller to more plugins and accept the larger compatibility and security surface as an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow external contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved or manifest-declared methods/capabilities with caller attribution, trust-tier behavior, docs, and focused contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the current trusted-only Gateway runtime caller and is the strongest history match for the permanent Plugin SDK/Gateway boundary decision.
